ideas.title: The cart drives itself on a long cord
ideas.critique: This is the first post where the motor leaves its block and something goes somewhere, which breaks a streak of five 'motor runs alone on its block' films. Belt slip by capstan, wheels digging in WheelSand and a tether that yanks back both ways are all general mechanisms that other builds can use. The weak spot is the payoff: the cord running out is one event, and if the pots sliding off the table is the whole climax, the player's only real choice is a length.

ideas.title: Will it make the top: the stall is the game
ideas.critique: This is round 1's winch idea with the single-ramp rig taken out. A 3D tether hooked anywhere, contacts per wheel on the heightfield and a drum radius that grows with the wound rope make the stall the motor's own answer, and permanent varnish damage gives the switch-off a cost the player remembers. The danger is the coil heating: if it turns into the copper-wire burnout post again with smoke particles and a 'weaker' flag, instead of a lower k the motor really runs with, it repeats 'Where I rushed it'.

ideas.title: Let it roll back: the motor brakes the cart and charges the pots
ideas.critique: The switch with three positions (pots, short, open) is a real choice whose result the existing back-EMF model already decides, and a runaway cart rattling off the planks is the kind of nerdy slapstick that works because the physics is honest. It depends on a winch haul that is not built yet. The pots growing bluer as they charge will be one fitted mass-balance number unless the round-1 pot chemistry exists, so a session spent here mostly shows that the winch's sign can flip.
